audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 1, 2, 3 and 5 read 'Skill' while their own why text says concede the chip, he out-trades you decisively, he all-ins you, and he stays ahead. Row 4 reads Zaahen while whys[4] says 'Level 6 evens things'.
audit.why: Packet chart is [Skill, Zaahen, Zaahen, Zaahen, Skill, Zaahen, Zaahen] on a 658-game sample at 46.66% — the largest and most trustworthy sample in this slice. The prose agrees with the packet on every one of those five rows; only the chart disagrees.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 2, 3, 5 to Zaahen and row 4 to Skill, as one atomic pair-matched group.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[] has only 3 entries where 4 are expected, and the three that exist are out of order (Lvl 6, Teamfights, Lvl 1) with no late-game entry at all.
audit.why: The missing spike is his, and it is the most important one on the page: Zaahen's passive states that when filled with Determination he gains bonus Attack Damage and can revive. Nothing anywhere on this matchup mentions that he comes back. A Neeko who spends a 120/105/90s Pop Blossom to kill him and then watches him stand up has lost the fight she just won.
audit.corrected: Added spikes[3] (text and when) for his revive window using before: null, since there is nothing on disk to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup-defining ability is literally called 'Ultimate' throughout — focus.text, loading, winCon, enemyWin, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull, report[5], report[9]. No Zaahen ability is named anywhere except one loose 'Darkin Glaive'.
audit.why: From the missing-interactions data the real names are The Darkin Glaive (Q), Aureate Rush (E) and Grim Deliverance (R). Mechanically: Q is an auto-reset that slashes twice, heals him, and can be recast to knock you up, on 10/9/8/7/6s; W is an 850-range stab that pulls you toward him on 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s; E is the dash and its damage scales with your maximum health, on 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s; R heals him for a portion of damage dealt, on 110/95/80s. The gap-closer you actually have to count is E, not the ultimate.
audit.corrected: Named Q, E and R where each drives the decision, and pointed the do's at Aureate Rush's 8s rather than a nameless 'big cooldown'.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal is never mentioned in either layer, and report[8] does not carry it either.
audit.why: Zaahen heals off both The Darkin Glaive and Grim Deliverance, and E's damage scales with your max health, so stacking HP makes his burst bigger rather than smaller. Grievous Wounds timing, not resistances, is what decides extended trades here.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal folded into whys[5]; the max-health scaling stated in whys[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d calls his spent ultimate a 'fifteen-second invitation'; Grim Deliverance is 110/95/80s.
audit.why: A ten-times-understated cooldown turns a real punish window into bad advice in both directions.

edits.before: His big cooldown — punish the gap while it is down. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: Aureate Rush (E) is the dash, back in 8s at rank 5 — count it before you step up.

edits.before: Zaahen burns Ultimate on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Zaahen burns Grim Deliverance on nothing — that is an 80s gap at rank 3.

edits.before: At 2 his Darkin Glaive lets him tax a fragile, low-durability Neeko for free — concede the chip.
edits.after: At 2 The Darkin Glaive (Q) taxes a fragile Neeko for free and heals him back — concede the chip.

edits.before: At 3 his Q and E out-trade you decisively — you have no early tankiness to stand in the exchange.
edits.after: At 3 the Q knockup recast and Aureate Rush out-trade you — E scales on your maximum health.

edits.before: By first item he stays ahead — you remain squishy and simply lose the 1v1 duel.
edits.after: By first item he stays ahead — Q and R both heal him, so anti-heal or skip the duel.
His revive: once Determination fills, Zaahen gains bonus AD and can come back up — hold Grievous Wounds and only commit Pop Blossom where your team can finish the second kill.
